title: Making Decisions Checkpoint
intro: Your programs can now take different paths: if, else, chains, nesting, switch and the conditional operator. Twelve rounds, one from every idea in this module. First-try answers earn three stars!

rounds.prompt: What can go inside the round brackets of an `if`?
options: Something that gives true or false, or a number, where 0 counts as false
The instruction you want to run
rounds.explain: Comparisons, logical expressions and bool variables are the normal choice. C++ also accepts any number, treating 0 as false and everything else as true.

rounds.prompt: The player has 3 lives. What does this print?
rounds.explain: A single `=` stores 1 in `lives`, and 1 counts as true, so the block runs. The famous fix is `==`, which asks the question instead.

rounds.prompt: This congratulates a score of 20. What is missing?
options: An else before the second cout
Braces: without them only the first instruction belongs to the if
rounds.explain: C++ ignores indentation. Only one instruction attaches to a braceless `if`, so the second `cout` always runs.

rounds.prompt: Marks are 80. How many lines does this print?
rounds.explain: A chain stops at the first true test. 80 is also 60 or more, but C++ never reaches that test once B has matched.

rounds.prompt: Top marks of 95 come out as a D. What is wrong?
options: The chain needs a final else
The loosest test is first, so nothing below it can ever run
rounds.explain: Every mark of 40 or more matches the first test. Range tests have to be ordered from narrowest to widest.

rounds.prompt: `int price;` is declared with no value, and a chain sets it, but no branch matches. What does `cout << price;` print?
options: A garbage number left over in memory
Nothing: the program refuses to compile
rounds.explain: C++ does not check that every path sets a variable. End the chain with a plain `else`, and start variables with a value such as `int price = 0;`.

rounds.prompt: Both conditions must be true and there is nothing to do in between. Which is better?
rounds.explain: `&&` gives one condition and one level of indentation. Nesting is for when each branch needs to do something different.

rounds.prompt: There is no break after case 1. What does this print?
rounds.explain: This is fall-through: C++ runs the matching case and keeps going downwards until it meets a `break`.

rounds.prompt: Which of these can a C++ switch NOT match?
rounds.explain: A switch needs a whole number or a `char`. Text, ranges and comparisons belong in an `else if` chain.

rounds.prompt: Age is 30. What does this store in price?
rounds.explain: The condition is false, so the conditional operator chooses the value after the colon. Read it as: condition ? whenTrue : whenFalse.

rounds.prompt: Match each tool to the job it fits best.

pairs.right: Do something only when a condition holds
The path taken when the if was false
A detail that applies inside one branch
Match one value against fixed options
Choose between two values in one line

rounds.explain: Six tools, six shapes of decision. Choosing the one that fits is most of what makes code readable.

rounds.prompt: Build a grade chain that works: highest band first, then the rest, ending with a catch-all.
rounds.explain: The narrowest test has to come first, because the chain stops at the first true condition. The closing `else` catches everything left and guarantees `grade` is always given a value.
